control_plan.implementation_approach:
Add a read-only memory settings endpoint such as `GET /settings/memory` in `service-gateway`, returning Hermes memory, user profile, updated timestamps, source identifiers, character counts, byte sizes, and quota usage.
Implement the backend service by reusing the existing Hermes memory and user profile storage or configuration access paths; do not introduce write operations in this iteration.
Calculate character usage with Unicode rune counting and report byte size separately with UTF-8 byte length; avoid estimating character count from token count or byte length.
Define shared frontend types for memory content, profile content, usage metrics, quotas, and API errors.
Register the new page at `/settings/memory` and add a “记忆” entry to the settings navigation, protected by the same permission model as other dashboard configuration pages.
Build the page with existing React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and shadcn patterns: separate panels for Hermes memory, user profile, and character usage; responsive layout; loading skeletons; empty states; error states; refresh action; and monospace content viewers with stable scroll areas.
Show character usage as numeric values plus progress bars, with clear states for no quota, near-limit, over-limit, and unavailable quota information.
Use existing localization files for all visible text and ensure the page remains usable on mobile and desktop without text overflow or layout shift.
Keep the page read-only and avoid exposing credentials or unrelated internal identifiers; return only fields needed by the dashboard.
Update the OpenAPI specification and keep the frontend API client generated or manually aligned with the documented contract.
Verify with focused frontend tests and service-gateway tests, then run the repository’s configured lint, typecheck, and test commands before handoff.
